nodes.description:
Fibroid vasculature is organized differently from that of a malignant solid tumor. The fibroid mass itself is poorly vascularized and is instead supplied by a highly vascularized pseudocapsule that develops in response to its growth and appears as a peripheral "ring of fire" on Doppler ultrasound. The angiogenic drive is attributed principally to the insulin-like growth factor system rather than to the HIF-1-alpha/VEGF axis of hypoxic tumors, and HIF-1-alpha has been reported absent from fibroids where it is readily demonstrable in leiomyosarcoma - which is what establishes that the common fibroid does not use the hypoxia route, and is not contradicted by the pseudohypoxia node, whose HIF stabilization is metabolite-driven and confined to the uncommon FH-deficient subtype. Separately, the growing mass raises interstitial pressure and obstructs venous drainage, enlarging the endometrial and myometrial venous lakes. Both the structurally deficient pseudocapsule vessels and the dilated venous lakes are proposed sources of the heavy bleeding, and which of them dominates is unsettled.
One correction the source makes about its own history is worth keeping: the interstitial-pressure explanation for the enlarged venous lakes was later challenged, with growth factors rather than mechanical pressure held largely responsible for enlarging the veins. The pressure account is recorded here because the microradiographic observation of enlarged lakes stands; its mechanical explanation does not.
nodes.id: Aberrant Pseudocapsule Angiogenesis and Venous Ectasia

nodes.description: A fibroid large enough to enlarge and deform the uterus displaces the structures around it. Anterior and fundal tumors press on the bladder, producing urinary frequency and, when the ureters are involved, hydronephrosis; posterior tumors press on the rectum, producing constipation; a large fibroid can go further and cause urinary obstruction or, rarely, hydronephrosis. This is the one arm of the mechanism that is purely a consequence of volume and position: severity correlates with fibroid size, number and anatomical placement rather than with driver genotype, and the treatments that shrink or remove the tumor relieve it while the treatments that only control bleeding do not.

nodes.description:
Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) originate as monoclonal tumors from a single myometrial smooth muscle cell (or a myometrial stem cell acquiring tumor-initiating features) that acquires a recurrent somatic driver mutation. The most common driver is a MED12 exon-2 mutation (~70-77%), followed by HMGA2/HMGA1 overexpression or chromosomal rearrangement (~10%, 12q14-15), biallelic FH (fumarate hydratase) loss defining the FH-deficient subtype (also seen in hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer, HLRCC), with rarer collagen IV (COL4A5/COL4A6) deletions also reported. Heterozygous MED12 mutations disrupt the CDK8/CDK19 kinase module of the Mediator complex, altering the chromatin landscape, enhancer engagement, genomic stability, and progesterone responsiveness.
Scoping decision, recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight: COL4A5/COL4A6 deletion and the SRCAP-complex class are named here but are deliberately not given has_subtypes entries. Both are recurrent but rare relative to the three modelled classes, neither has a distinct pathophysiology arm this entry could populate beyond the shared ECM output, and neither changes management. A curator with a collagen-IV-specific mechanism or frequency source should add the subtype then.

nodes.description:
Fibroids do not bleed only by mechanics. Fibroid tissue secretes TGF-beta-3 in response to ovarian steroids, and TGF-beta-3 acts on the overlying endometrium to downregulate BMP receptor 2 (which the source says is likely to cause defective decidualization) and to reduce expression of plasminogen activator inhibitor 1, antithrombin III and thrombomodulin, which the source says likely contributes to the bleeding. Both steps are hedged in the source and are hedged here. Note also that two of those three regulators are anticoagulants, so the net direction is an interpretation of the hemostatic outcome the source draws rather than a reading of each protein in isolation - the DECREASED modifier on the blood-coagulation process below records that net outcome, not a per-protein reading. The endometrium is therefore both less able to decidualize and less able to form and hold a hemostatic plug. This node is where the reproductive and the bleeding phenotypes share a mechanism.
Scope note: the purely physical contributions to the bleeding - increased endometrial surface area, disordered myometrial contractility, and venous ectasia from compression - are real and are cited below, but they are properties of the tumor mass and belong to the Tumor Growth and Bulk Compression nodes. This node is the endometrial signalling arm, which is why it is tagged TISSUE.
nodes.id: Endometrial Hemostatic Failure and Impaired Vessel Closure

nodes.description: The defining feature of a fibroid is not its cell count but its matrix: the mutated smooth muscle cells and the adjacent tumor-associated fibroblasts deposit disproportionate quantities of collagen, fibronectin and proteoglycans, which constitute a substantial fraction of tumor volume. The accumulated matrix is not inert. It stiffens the tissue, and it binds and prolongs the activity of the growth factors (TGF-beta chief among them) that drove its own deposition, so the matrix becomes a self-reinforcing feed-forward arm of the mechanism rather than the end of it. Matrix metalloproteinase activity is dysregulated in parallel, so remodeling as well as deposition is abnormal. This is the node on which the disease's name rests and the one that distinguishes a fibroid from a simple hyperplasia.

nodes.description: Estradiol and progesterone are essential for fibroid growth. During each ovulatory cycle the myometrium proliferates under ovarian steroid stimulation. Progesterone, acting through its nuclear receptor (PGR) in differentiated fibroid cells, activates paracrine secretion of WNT ligands, cytokines, and growth factors that drive a small stem cell population to proliferate. Fibroids rarely arise before menarche and frequently regress after menopause, underscoring steroid hormone dependence. The excessive matrix these proliferating cells and the adjacent tumor-associated fibroblasts lay down is modelled as the separate downstream node "Excessive Extracellular Matrix Deposition and Tissue Stiffening"; this node is the cell-population expansion alone.

With the HIF prolyl hydroxylases inhibited by fumarate, HIF-alpha escapes degradation and a hypoxia transcriptional programme runs in a normoxic cell. This is the FH subtype's distinctive route to the tumor's distorted, staghorn vasculature.
Read this alongside the angiogenesis node, which records HIF-1-alpha as absent from uterine fibroids. The two are not in conflict but the boundary matters: that observation comes from unselected fibroids, which are overwhelmingly MED12- or HMGA2-driven, and it is what establishes that the common fibroid does NOT use the hypoxia/VEGF route. Pseudohypoxia is specific to the uncommon FH-deficient subtype, where it is driven by a metabolite rather than by low oxygen. A reader who took the pseudohypoxia claim to apply to fibroids generally would have it backwards.

nodes.description:
Pregnancy loss in fibroid-complicated pregnancies. The cited meta-analysis reports miscarriage rather than recurrent miscarriage, and does not attribute it to cavity distortion, so neither qualifier is claimed here; the recurrent framing comes from the phenotype concept, not from this source. A meta-analysis of 24 studies found fibroids raised miscarriage risk in unadjusted analysis; after adjustment for confounders the significant obstetric associations were preterm birth, cesarean delivery, placenta previa, placental abruption, postpartum hemorrhage, intrauterine fetal death, breech presentation and preeclampsia, and miscarriage was not among them. Both results are recorded here because the distinction matters for how strongly this phenotype should be claimed.
The ontology binding is deliberately omitted. HP:0200067 Recurrent spontaneous abortion means exactly this, but it sits under HP:0032443 (past medical history) rather than under HP:0000118 (phenotypic abnormality), so it is not a member of the PhenotypeTerm dynamic enum; HP:0005268 Miscarriage and HP:0003826 Stillbirth are both outside the enum root too, under the clinical-modifier branch. Binding a term that means something else would be worse than leaving it unbound, so the meaning is carried by preferred_term. Asherman_Syndrome records the same gap for the same term (issue #7837, gap 3).

nodes.description: Progressive growth of the leiomyoma produces a benign smooth muscle tumor of the uterus. Submucosal and intramural tumors distort the endometrial cavity and impair hemostasis, causing heavy menstrual bleeding and consequent iron deficiency anemia. Bulk from larger tumors compresses adjacent pelvic organs (bladder, rectum), causing pressure symptoms, while distortion of the cavity and tubal ostia contributes to reproductive morbidity. Most affected women are asymptomatic: fibroids cause clinically significant disease in roughly a quarter of reproductive-age women overall, and affect quality of life in approximately 30% of cases.
